summary.name: Agent4Rec
summary.one_liner: Agent4Rec is a recommender-system user simulator that uses LLM-powered generative agents, initialized from real datasets, to mimic how users interact with recommendations.
use_cases: Simulating user behavior to evaluate recommender algorithms offline
Reproducing filter bubble effects in recommendation
Studying causal relationships in recommendation tasks
Comparing simulated agent preferences with real user tastes
Bridging gaps between offline metrics and online performance
summary.what_it_does: Agent4Rec is a user simulator in which each agent has a profile module initialized from real-world datasets (such as MovieLens, Steam, and Amazon-Book) that captures tastes and social traits. Its memory module logs factual and emotional memories with an emotion-driven reflection mechanism. Its action module supports taste-driven and emotion-driven behaviors. Agents interact with a pre-implemented collaborative filtering recommender in a page-by-page manner. The authors evaluate how faithfully the agents align with user-personalized preferences, and they use it to emulate the filter bubble effect and explore causal relationships.
notable: LLM-driven generative agents with profile, memory, and action modules tailored to recommenders
Profiles initialized from real datasets like MovieLens, Steam, and Amazon-Book
Emotion-driven reflection and emotion-driven actions alongside taste-driven ones
caveats: Relies on a collaborative filtering-based recommendation algorithm; the page notes deviations between agents and real user preferences
Page describes capabilities and limitations but states no specific accuracy figures in the abstract
